Identifying dynamic obstacles, people walking into the crops area, is important for preventing and ensuring the safety of people/animals and also to guarantee the continuity of the pro- cess. Our proposal is based on image processing analysis supported by the combination of spectral segmentation and temporal dif- ferences. Firstly, obstacle detection is performed in the spatial scale and then, a temporal differencing is carried out for motion detection. This approach addresses the problem of uncertainty in uncontrolled outdoor agricultural and dynamical scenarios involv- ing agricultural machinery. Although the proposed approach could be considered deterministic in nature, the high variability in the illumination conditions, camera vibrations, unknown and unex- pected static or dynamic objects introduce the aforementioned uncertainty. Hence, the proposed computer vision approach deals with differences in initial conditions, belonging to a kind of systems with a chaotic deterministic behaviour in the context of applied soft computing in agricultural machinery. The experimental results show that our method is suitable and effective in the context of our agricultural scenarios. We also show that trees detection is possible from the point of view of image analysing processing, making it a useful contribution for path localization and path mapping tasks. More speciﬁcally, another important contribution is that no training process is required. It is entirely based on a combination of digital and image analysis techniques. Scenarios analysed include static and non-static obstacles having an average classiﬁcation rate of 91.0%. In contrast to their work, our methodology does not require a train- ing process; obstacles might appear on scene from the beginning. Biber et al. [30] incorporated a LIDAR (Light Detection And Ran- ging) sensor for range ﬁnding in their navigation system to detect unexpected objects. Each tractor in the ﬂeet of RHEA was equipped with a LIDAR system to detect, localize, and classify trees with the aim of safe navigation with favourable assessment [31]. The main advantage of LIDAR sensors is that they are not inﬂuenced by sunlight with high infra-red radiation content, which is not fully achieved with Kinect sensors. Despite the effectiveness of these LIDAR-based systems, different researches have demonstrated the outperformance of combined LIDAR and vision systems particularly in dynamic outdoor scenarios [32–34] . In [35], authors develop an obstacle detection system using stereo matching to generate a point cloud at regions in the image.
